title: Cap. X: Retorsion — if prior reatus is only by will, why Christ’s suffering?
pass_a_gloss: I could also turn this reason back upon its author. For if where there is no evil there is no need of a remedy, and there is no evil if there is in us no reatus prior to our original blot on account of Adam's disobedience, and the true and only cause why that reatus is in us is God's will — I do not understand what necessity there is of imputed justice. Let God only abstain from imputing the first Adam's sin, as He refrains from imputing other sins, whether Adam's own or our ancestors', and there will be no evil, nor need of a remedy. For there is no cause, if Garissoles is believed, why God should impute that sin to us rather than other sins, whether Adam's or other parents', except His will alone. Since therefore it hangs on His will whether to impute or not, what need was there that Christ suffer so dreadfully so that that sin might not be imputed to us?
pass_b_english: I can turn the argument on its maker. If no evil means no need of a remedy, and there is no evil unless we carry a guilt earlier than our original stain from Adam’s disobedience, and the sole true cause of that guilt in us is God’s will — then I cannot see why imputed justice is necessary at all. Let God simply withhold imputation of the first Adam’s sin, as He already withholds imputation of other sins — Adam’s own, or our forefathers’ — and there will be no evil and no need of a remedy. On Garissoles’s account there is no reason God should charge us with that sin rather than with Adam’s other sins or other parents’ sins, except His bare will. If imputing or not imputing hangs on that will alone, why did Christ have to suffer such horrors so that this sin might not be charged to us?
source_text: Possem etiam hanc rationem in suum autorem retorquere. Nam si ubi nullum est malum, nullo opus est remedio, & nullum sit malum, si nullus sit in nobis propter Adae inobedientiam reatus labe nostra originali prior, & cur sit in nobis iste reatus vera & unica causa est Dei voluntas, non intelligo quae sit imputatae justitiae necessitas. Abstineat modo Deus ab imputatione primi Adae peccati quemadmodum sibi temperat ab aliorum peccatorum, vel ipsius Adami, vel nostrorum majorum, imputatione, nullum erit malum, nec opus erit remedio. Nulla enim est causa, si D. Garissolio fides habetur, cur Deus illud peccatum nobis potius quam alia peccata, vel Adami, vel aliorum parentum, imputet, praeter unam eius voluntatem. Cum ergo id pendeat ab eius voluntate ut imputet, vel non imputet, quid opus fuit, Christum tam dira pati, ut posset nobis illud peccatum non imputari?
